verification.note: Confirmed by reading. MobileInspectorSheet.tsx:206-219 returns only the peek strip when !expanded, and `children` is rendered only inside the Drawer at :282. FileDetailShell.tsx:196-204 passes `mobileSheet ?? inspector` as those children, so going to peek unmounts InspectorShell and every inspector-tabs SlotEntryRenderer (ShellLayout.tsx:326-341). AskTab.tsx:246-248 runs `releaseAskEntry(fileId)` on unmount. askStore.ts:117-127 aborts the controller and, when status === 'streaming', calls entries.delete(fileId). The ask loop then returns early on the aborted signal (AskTab.tsx:291/308/315), so nothing writes the entry back and the question and partial answer are lost. Crossing the breakpoint switches between two different InspectorShell elements (ShellLayout.tsx:344-359, FileDetailShell.tsx:194 vs :203), which remounts the tab with the same result. Spec 056 step 6 (docs/specs/ask-about-this-file.md:131-135) and I11 require these to be kept. Related path: a pill click calls lowerInspector (AskTab.tsx:410, FileDetailShell.tsx:144-149). The citations event arrives before meta/done, so clicking a pill in that window also drops the sheet to peek and deletes the streaming entry. Closing the desktop pane (FileDetailShell.tsx:194) unmounts the tab in the same way.

Confirmed. askStore.ts:36 declares `const entries = new Map` at module scope. releaseAskEntry (askStore.ts:117-127) keeps every non-streaming entry and only clears its controller. dropAskEntry (askStore.ts:105-111) is called only from AskTab.tsx:238-244, when fileId changes within one mount. When the file page unmounts, only releaseAskEntry runs, so an answered or failed entry stays. A later visit to the same fileId reads it back through getAskEntry (AskTab.tsx:191-195) and shows the old question and answer. This contradicts spec 056 step 6 (docs/specs/ask-about-this-file.md:134-135): leaving the file page drops the file's entry, and returning shows an empty tab.

Confirmed. file_question.py:34 `_CITATION_MARKER = re.compile(r"\[(\d{1,3})\]")` does not match `[1000]`: the `]` must follow at most three digits. citations() (file_question.py:211-216) therefore never emits n >= 1000. The prompt numbers passages with an unbounded `loop.index` (prompts/rag/file_question_user.jinja2:6). On the frontend, AnswerText splits on `\[\d+\]` (AskTab.tsx:145-149) and returns null for a number missing from the citations map, so the valid marker disappears from the text. This is reachable in normal use. The budget may be set as high as 200,000 (config.py:801-828, search-config.yml.example:352), and refine re-chunks transcripts into single sentences (refine.py:310-323). A long refined transcript under a raised budget can therefore send more than 999 chunks. Under the 16,000 default, more than 999 chunks would require an average of about 16 characters per chunk.

The divergence is real. available() (file_question.py:80-89) checks EXISTS on transcript_chunks/fts_text_content with no text filter. load_material skips rows with falsy text (file_question.py:165-166, 180-181) and returns None when no rows remain (file_question.py:192-193). The router turns None into a 404 (routers/rag.py:352-353). Reachability looks narrow. The writers I checked filter empty text before storing: extractors/base.py:103 returns [] for blank text, whisper segments are stripped and kept only when non-empty (whisper.py:447-448), and words are filtered at whisper.py:587-589. refine.py:342 builds chunks from `w.text or ""`, so an empty-text chunk is not ruled out there, but I did not find a path that produces one. Whitespace-only text passes both checks, so the two functions agree on that case.

specification_compliance: Spec 056 step 6 / I11 (keep the entry across a sheet close or a breakpoint crossing): violated, see ASK-1.
Spec 056 step 6 (leaving the file page drops the entry; returning shows an empty tab): violated, see ASK-2.
I3 (only sent chunk numbers are cited): holds, because citations() bounds n by len(chunks). Valid numbers of 1000 or more are dropped (ASK-3).
I6 vs the question route: the availability check and load_material disagree on what counts as a text chunk (ASK-4).
potential_unspecified_behavior: Closing the desktop inspector pane (ctrl+\) while an answer streams unmounts the tab and deletes the entry. The spec does not list a desktop pane close among the cases that keep the entry, but it says the entry lives while the file page is mounted.
A pill clicked after `citations` arrives and before `done` calls lowerInspector. On mobile this unmounts the tab and deletes the still-streaming entry.
regression_risks: A fix for ASK-1 that keeps streaming entries on release must still abort and drop them on a fileId change or a page unmount, or the semaphore slot leaks (I11).
test_coverage: I did not inspect whether AskTab.test.tsx covers unmount during streaming or remounting after leaving the page.
not_verified: Did not run any tests or a browser; all four claims were checked by reading the code.
Did not check whether InspectorShell keeps hidden panels mounted across tab switches; this does not affect the sheet/peek path.
Did not trace every transcription provider and the refine aligner exhaustively for empty-text chunk rows (ASK-4 reachability).
Did not measure real chunk counts for long refined transcripts (ASK-3 reachability).
